title: Direct Synthesis of Gold Nanoparticles on Cysteine-rich Tags in Yeast Cells
protocol: Grow S. pombe cells in liquid EMM at 30°C overnight.
Measure OD600 reach to ~1.0 with a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Harvest 10 mL of the culture into a 15mL centrifuge tube for centrifugation at 2000 rpm for 2 min to obtain a cell pellet.
Disperse the cell pellet with 1 ml of PBS buffer.
Transfer to a 1.5ml microtube for centrifugation at 2000 rpm for 2 min to obtain a final cell pellet for further EM experiments.
Fast inject 1 mL of -60°C methanol into the microtube.
Dispense instantly by pipetting for 1 minute.
Centrifuge at 3000 rpm for 1 minute to remove supernatant.
Disperse with 1 mL of PBS-A.
Oxidize in 1 mL of 3 or 5 mM DTDPA in PBS (or 0.1M PIPES) for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Chemically fix by adding 20 µL of 25% GA to the tube for 30 min fixation at 4°C (for Scheme 2a and 2b).
Centrifuge to remove supernatant (at 2000 rpm for 2 minutes) after oxidization.
Add 1 mL of ice-cold 5 mM DTDPA and 4% PFA in PIPES buffer, incubate at 4°C for 30 min.
Centrifuge again to remove supernatant (at 2000 rpm for 2 minutes).
Neutralize excess aldehyde with 1 mL of 50mM glycine in PBS or PIPES buffer overnight at 4°C.
Centrifuge to obtain a cellpellet at 2000 rpm for 2 minutes.
Wash with PBS three times, each for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge to remove the supernatant.
Fast inject 1 mL of 4 °C methanol into the microtube.
Disperse the cell pellet instantly by pipetting for 1 minute.
Centrifuge at 3000 rpm for 1 minute to remove the supernatant.
Incubate with 1 mL of 0.2 mg/mL zymolyase-20T in PBS (or in 0.1 M PIPES) at room temperature for approximately 30 minutes.
Check under microscope to ensure cells are properly digested as dull gray.
Permeabilize with 1 mL of 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Wash with 1 mL of PBS-A three times, each for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge at 2000 rpm for 2 minutes to obtain the cell pellet.
Disperse the cell pellet with 1 mL PBS-A.
Prepare the mixture for AuNP synthesis.
Place the cell pellet into a 0.05 mm deep aluminum carrier.
Cap a 3 mm x 0.16 mm sapphire disc (pre-soaked with 1-hexadecene) quickly onto the aluminum carrier.
Load the capped carrier into the customized HPF specimen holder for high pressure freezing.
Unload the carrier under liquid nitrogen in the foam cryobox.
Store the unloaded carrier in 2 mL polypropylene microcentrifuge tubes in liquid nitrogen before use.
Load 10-12 specimens (in aluminum carriers) into a 2 mL polypropylene microtube with 1 mL of frozen freeze-substitution solvent under liquid nitrogen.
Transfer the microtube to the pre-cooled to -90°C chamber of a Leica AFS2 freeze-substitution machine for FSF processing.
Keep the specimens in 1 mL of acetone containing 3 or 5 mM DTDPA + 3% ddH₂O at -90°C for 12h.
Warm up gradually from 90°C to -30°C within 6h.
Stay at -30°C for 2h.
Add 50 µL of 10% GA (in acetone) to the microtube containing the DTDPA solution at -30°C for 5 h fixation.
Take out the aluminum carriers and sapphire discs using forceps tip to separate cell pellet from carrier, leaving cells in the solution.
Gradually rehydrate:
Change to 1mL -30 °C 5% ddH₂O in acetone, wait for 30 min.
Change to 1mL -30 °C 30% ddH₂O in acetone, wait for 30 min.
Warm up gradually from -30 °C to -20 °C within 30 min.
Warm up gradually from -20 °C to 4 °C, add 3 x 100 µL of pre-frozen PBS drops (next drop added upon previous drop dissolve completely) within 30 min.
Add 700 µL of ice-cold PBS for 10 min at 4 °C.
Centrifuge at 2000 rpm for 2 min.
Change to 1 mL of 50 mM glycine in PBS for neutralization at 4°C overnight.
Wash with 1 mL PBS-A for 5 min × 3.
Keep the specimen in 1 mL of acetone at -90 °C for 3 h.
Change the medium to 1 mL of acetone containing 50 mM DTDPA + 0.02% TA + 5% ddH₂O at -90°C and stay for 20 h.
Warm up gradually from -90°C to -60°C within 5 h.
Stay at -60°C for 10 h.
Warm up gradually from -60°C to -35°C within 5 h.
Change to 1 mL of acetone containing 0.25% GA + 0.01% UA + 50 mM DTDPA + 5% ddH₂O at -35°C for 5 h fixation.
Detach cells from the carrier and sapphire disc, and take out the carrier and disc from the microtube with forceps.
Gradually rehydrate by gently adding or sucking off solution using a syringe or pipette tip.
Cool down the HEPES buffer to -35°C and wait for 30 min.
Warm up from -35°C to 0°C within 10 min.
Add 1 mL of RT 0.2 M HEPES buffer containing 50 mM glycine.
Neutralize with 1 mL of 50 mM glycine in PBS at 4°C overnight.
Wash with 1 mL of PBS-A for 3 x 5 min, centrifuge at 2000 rpm × 2 min to obtain cell pellet.
Add 4.28 µL of 2-ME into the microtube containing yeast cells dispersed in 1 mL of PBS-A and incubate at RT for 1 h.
Add 50 µL of 10 mM HAuCl₄ to the microtube, immediately vortex; Add 100 µL of 500 mM D-P, vortex; Incubate for 2 h at 4°C.
Add 20 µL of 100 mM NaBH₄, immediately shake to mix well, incubate for 5 min.
Centrifuge at 2000 rpm for 2 min to obtain cell pellet.
Add 1 mL of PBS-A and keep at 4°C.
Centrifuge at 2000rpm for 2 minutes to obtain cell pellet.
Fill the pre-cleaned 0.1 or 0.05 mm deep aluminum carrier with cell pellet.
Cap a 3 mm x 0.16 mm sapphire disc (pre-soaked with 1-hexadecene) quickly onto the aluminum carrier.
Load the capped carrier into the HPF specimen holder for high pressure freezing.
Unload the carrier under liquid nitrogen in the foam cryobox and store in 2mL polypropylene microcentrifuge tubes in liquid nitrogen before use.
Transfer the microtube containing 1% UA under LN₂ to the pre-cooled -90°C chamber of a Leica AFS2 freeze-substitution machine and stay for 24 hours at -90 °C.
Warm up gradually from -90°C to -60°C within 5 hours.
Hold at -60°C for 6 hours.
Warm up gradually from -60°C to -20°C within 3 hours.
Hold at -20°C for 18 hours.
Warm up gradually from -20°C to 4°C within 2 hours.
Wash with acetone three times for one hour each at 4°C.
Warm up to room temperature for resin infiltration.
Immerse the sample in 50% GA under LN₂.
Transfer the microtube to the pre-cooled -90°C chamber of a Leica AFS2 freeze-substitution machine and incubate for 12 hours at -90°C.
Gradually warm up from -90°C to -60°C over 6 hours.
Wash with acetone three times, each for one hour at -60°C.
Separate the specimen from aluminum carriers using a fine tip at -60°C.
Add 10 µL of 1% HAuCl₄ (in acetone) to the microtube containing 1 mL of acetone and incubate for 8 hours at -60°C.
Add 10 µL of fresh 10 mM NaBH₄ to the solution and enhance gold for 20 hours at -60°C.
Wash with acetone three times, each for one hour at -60°C.
Change to 1 mL of 1% OsO₄ + 0.1% UA in acetone and fix for 5 hours at -60°C.
Warm up gradually from -60°C to -30°C over 5 hours.
Warm up gradually from -30°C to 4°C over 2 hours.
Wash with acetone three times, each for one hour at 4°C.
Warm up the sample to room temperature for resin infiltration.
Infiltrate the sample with 1:1 SPI-Pon 812 resin:acetone for 1.5 hours on a rotator.
Continue infiltrating with 3:1 SPI-Pon 812 resin:acetone for 6-12 hours on a rotator.
Infiltrate the sample with 100% SPI-Pon 812 resin for one hour on a rotator.
Infiltrate the sample with 100% SPI-Pon 812 resin for three hours on a rotator.
Embed and polymerize the sample in 100% SPI-Pon 812 resin for one hour on a rotator.
Transfer the resin infiltrated sample attached on the sapphire disc to a flat-tip BEEM embedding capsule.
Incubate the capsule in fresh resin for 12 hours at 45°C.
Continue incubation of the capsule at 60°C for 24-48 hours.
Trim the polymerized specimen carefully to expose the sapphire disc.
Dip the trimmed sample into liquid nitrogen (LN₂) for 10 seconds.
Detach the cells from the disc using forceps and separate the disc from the block.
Trim the block to a trapezoidal shape for thin sectioning.
Prepare sections on a 200-mesh hexagonal copper grid coated with/without formvar.
Place 90 nm thin sections on copper grids positive stained with 2% uranyl acetate (UA) for 6 minutes or use unstained sections directly.
Conduct EM imaging on an FEI Spirit electron microscope operating at 120kV.
Record images with a 4k x 4k 895 CCD camera under proper defocus values.
Use magnification ranging from 11kX to 30kX for visualizing AuNPs in cells.
